cohort: Patients who gave birth at a rural district hospital in northern KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa in 2018
finding: Caesarean delivery at a rural primary care setting was associated with a significantly higher risk of maternal and neonatal complications, including postpartum hemorrhage and neonatal nursery admission, compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was associated with a 25 times higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage and three times higher odds of any maternal complication compared to vaginal delivery.
